newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs pare gains in late trade on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: JGBs pare gains in late trade on profit-taking.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly higher on Tuesday after paring most gains toward the close.
"Stocks recovered toward the close, and this triggered profit-taking in JGBs from traders who had bought earlier based on a fall in share prices," a trader for a long-term credit bank said.

JGBs rose in the morning session after the release of the Economic Planning Agency's monthly report, which contained a cautious assessment of the economy, and they extended gains early in the afternoon, traders said.
The September ended at 126.50, up slightly from the previous day's close of 126.47. Turnover was 33,610 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.110 percent as of 0633 GMT, down slightly from Monday's close of 2.115 percent.
The firmness of JGBs in the afternoon was due to a sharp fall in Tokyo share prices and weaker-than-expected June household spending data, traders said.

Japan's household spending in June fell 4.7 percent in real terms from a year earlier,the government's Management and Coordination Agency said on Tuesday. Traders said the market had been expecting a fall of about 2.5 to three percent.
JGBs pared gains later in the afternoon as stocks staged a partial recovery and a large-lot sell order for the benchmark 182nd cash JGB capped the upside, traders said.
Traders said an offer of 100 billion yen worth of the 182nd 10-year JGB at 2.065 percent was detected in mid-afternoon.
"There was talk that the offer was from a foreign financial institution. I guess this means some people are reluctant to see rates fall further," a brokerage house trader said.
Comments by a senior government official that the JGB market is a bit too pessimistic about the outlook for the economy also weighed on the upside, traders said.

Referring to falling yields of Japanese government bonds, the official told Reuters: "The market is a bit too pessimistic about the outlook for the economy. It's not a situation that the downside risk for the economy is on the horizon."
The source added: "Ruling out the possibility of an interest rate rise within this year is a bit premature."

Asked about Monday's reported comments by EPA Minister Taro Aso about a possible rise in interest rates by the end of this year, the source said there were no discussions among government bodies about interest rates for now.
Regarding the EPA's monthly report released on Tuesday morning, an agency official told reporters that the negative effects of an April sales tax increase were still seen in July.
"We thought the negative impact would disappear in the April-June period, so we still need to see when such effects will vanish," he said.
The EPA report's cautious assessment of construction trends and the effects of the tax increase helped spur buying of JGBs in morning trade, a trust bank trader said.
